root_cause.text: `sbc_execute_unmap()` in `drivers/target/target_core_sbc.c` performed the UNMAP LBA+range bounds check without detecting 64-bit unsigned overflow, so a wrapped `lba + range` could bypass the device-capacity limit check.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (lba + range < lba || lba + range > dev->transport->get_blocks(dev) + 1)` and the commit message explicitly says the function “does not guard against LBA + range wrapping around on 64-bit overflow,” indicating the original check only compared against capacity and missed wraparound.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `if (lba + range < lba || lba + range > dev->transport->get_blocks(dev) + 1)` and the commit message explicitly says the function “does not guard against LBA + range wrapping around on 64-bit overflow,” indicating the original check only compared against capacity and missed wraparound.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix UNMAP range validation by detecting overflow in `lba + range` before performing the existing out-of-range check.
intent_record.what: In sbc_execute_unmap(), the bounds check on `lba + range` was changed from a single comparison against `dev->transport->get_blocks(dev) + 1` to a two-part condition that also checks whether `lba + range < lba` before the existing upper-bound test.
intent_record.how: This adds protection against unsigned integer overflow when computing `lba + range`. If the addition wraps around, the new check treats the request as out of range and aborts it instead of allowing a potentially invalid UNMAP operation to proceed.

grouping_result.intent: Fix UNMAP range validation by detecting overflow in `lba + range` before performing the existing out-of-range check.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the reported root cause: it adds overflow detection for the UNMAP `lba + range` calculation before the capacity bounds check, which is exactly the vulnerability condition.

candidates.rationale: This is the pre-fix bounds check that directly uses lba + range without first checking for 64-bit unsigned overflow, allowing wraparound to evade the device-capacity limit.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the pre-fix UNMAP bounds check that evaluates lba + range directly without first handling 64-bit unsigned overflow. If the addition wraps, the comparison can be bypassed and an out-of-range UNMAP request may be accepted.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the vulnerable bounds check in sbc_execute_unmap(): `if (lba + range > dev->transport->get_blocks(dev) + 1) { ... }`. This is exactly the unchecked 64-bit unsigned addition pattern described in the root cause, because `lba + range` can wrap before the comparison and bypass the capacity limit. The function does not contain any overflow-safe pre-check such as `range > limit - lba`, so the fix is not present here.
